correctness.rationale: Proof fixes the normalized graph-state amplitudes, obtains the flat reduced-state spectrum by finite-field character orthogonality, identifies the cut matrix as U_A^T U_B using simplicity, derives all unsigned-incidence left kernels including characteristic-two and odd-cycle cases, and calculates the exact rank as n-q_A-q_B+rank(T_A^T T_B). The Hamilton-path family checks the complement is connected nonbipartite and yields a one-unit characteristic-two deficit precisely for even n. Finite checker: 179427 exhaustive cases through five base vertices, 20000 random cases at 6..15, 112 Hamilton-path cases, and 10 direct reduced-state eigenspectra (max eigenvalue error 2.22e-16). Finite tests do not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: Closest full texts show the general cut-rank graph-state rule, high-dimensional qudit frameworks, two-colorable multipartite Schmidt measure, the full binary line-graph adjacency rank, and a cut-rank boundary upper bound. They do not state an exact all-edge-partition signed-component overlap law over every prime, nor the specified even-order complete-graph Hamilton-path qubit versus odd-prime maximality jump. The existing complete-bipartite rook-graph rectangular cut is a covered special case and is not independently claimed. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An earlier specialized finite-field incidence-rank, signed-graphic-matroid, or graph-state entanglement theorem may already imply the same signed component-overlap identity under another terminology.

The synthesis uses established graph-state cut-rank and elementary incidence-kernel techniques. Historical originality of the precise all-partition prime-characteristic formulation has not received independent expert review.

value.rationale: Exact full entanglement spectra for every edge bipartition of arbitrary simple base graph and every prime qudit dimension reduce to a matrix of connected-component overlaps on at most n vertices, rather than a potentially quadratic-size line-graph cut matrix; nonbipartite components cause an exact odd-characteristic transition. Hamilton-path cuts of K_n exhibit a natural, sharp qubit-only entanglement deficit for even n, with complete maximal mixing at every odd prime. This is a structurally motivated quantum-network classification beyond a known complete-bipartite rectangular-cut special case.
